title: Sending out the Twelve (and the Seventy)

en.9:35: Jesus went through all the towns and villages, teaching in their synagogues, preaching the gospel of the kingdom, and healing every disease and sickness.
en.9:36: When He saw the crowds, He was moved with compassion for them, because they were harassed and helpless, like sheep without a shepherd.
en.9:37: Then He said to His disciples, “The harvest is plentiful, but the workers are few.
en.9:38: Ask the Lord of the harvest, therefore, to send out workers into His harvest.”
en.10:5: These twelve Jesus sent out with the following instructions: “Do not go onto the road of the Gentiles or enter any town of the Samaritans.
en.10:6: Go rather to the lost sheep of Israel.
en.10:7: As you go, preach this message: ‘The kingdom of heaven is near.’
en.10:8: Heal the sick, raise the dead, cleanse the lepers, drive out demons. Freely you have received; freely give.
en.10:9: Do not take along any gold or silver or copper in your belts.
en.10:10: Take no bag for the road, or second tunic, or sandals, or staff; for the worker is worthy of his provisions.
en.10:11: Whatever town or village you enter, find out who is worthy there and stay at his house until you move on.
en.10:12: As you enter the home, greet its occupants.
en.10:13: If the home is worthy, let your peace rest on it, but if it is not, let your peace return to you.
en.10:14: And if anyone will not welcome you or heed your words, shake the dust off your feet when you leave that home or town.
en.10:15: Truly I tell you, it will be more bearable for Sodom and Gomorrah on the day of judgment than for that town.
en.10:16: Behold, I am sending you out like sheep among wolves; therefore be as shrewd as snakes and as innocent as doves.

en.6:7: Then Jesus called the Twelve to Him and began to send them out two by two, giving them authority over unclean spirits.
en.6:8: He instructed them to take nothing but a staff for the journey—no bread, no bag, no money in their belts—
en.6:9: and to wear sandals, but not a second tunic.
en.6:10: And He told them, “When you enter a house, stay there until you leave that area.
en.6:11: If anyone will not welcome you or listen to you, shake the dust off your feet when you leave that place, as a testimony against them.”
en.6:12: So they set out and preached that the people should repent.
en.6:13: They also drove out many demons and healed many of the sick, anointing them with oil.

en.9:1: Then Jesus called the Twelve together and gave them power and authority over all demons, and power to cure diseases.
en.9:2: And He sent them out to proclaim the kingdom of God and to heal the sick.
en.9:3: “Take nothing for the journey,” He told them, “no staff, no bag, no bread, no money, no second tunic.
en.9:4: Whatever house you enter, stay there until you leave that area.
en.9:5: If anyone does not welcome you, shake the dust off your feet when you leave that town, as a testimony against them.”
en.9:6: So they set out and went from village to village, preaching the gospel and healing people everywhere.
en.10:1: After this, the Lord appointed seventy-two others and sent them two by two ahead of Him to every town and place He was about to visit.
en.10:2: And He told them, “The harvest is plentiful, but the workers are few. Ask the Lord of the harvest, therefore, to send out workers into His harvest.
en.10:3: Go! I am sending you out like lambs among wolves.
en.10:4: Carry no purse or bag or sandals. Do not greet anyone along the road.
en.10:5: Whatever house you enter, begin by saying, ‘Peace to this house.’
en.10:6: If a man of peace is there, your peace will rest on him; if not, it will return to you.
en.10:7: Stay at the same house, eating and drinking whatever you are offered. For the worker is worthy of his wages. Do not move around from house to house.
en.10:8: If you enter a town and they welcome you, eat whatever is set before you.
en.10:9: Heal the sick who are there and tell them, ‘The kingdom of God is near you.’
en.10:10: But if you enter a town and they do not welcome you, go into the streets and declare,
en.10:11: ‘Even the dust of your town that clings to our feet, we wipe off as a testimony against you. Yet be sure of this: The kingdom of God is near.’
en.10:12: I tell you, it will be more bearable on that day for Sodom than for that town.
